validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed via an independent, highly authoritative primary source not previously cited on this row: the Egyptian Presidency's own official website (presidency.eg), filed under 'Presidential Openings and National Projects / Petroleum and Natural Gas', title 'Establishment of the Southwest Mleiha oil pipeline in the Western Desert.' Its body text: 'Establishing a pipeline to transport quantities of oil produced from the southwest Mleiha fields to the oil treatment station in the Mleiha area, estimated at about 7 thousand barrels/day, at a cost of 31 million dollars.' This matches GEM's Capacity (7,000 bpd), Cost ($31,000,000), StartLocation (Southwest Mleiha), and EndLocation (Mleiha) EXACTLY, and confirms Fuel=Oil. This is real infrastructure, not a GEM-only/hallucinated entity. CLASSIFICATION: correct as an oil pipeline; nothing suggests it is gas, NGL, or a non-pipeline facility. DUPLICATE CHECK (roster watchlist item 'P0572 Mleiha-El Hamra vs P5125 Southwest Mleiha - same trunk?'): NOT a duplicate. P0572 (Mleiha oilfield -> Matruh, 167 km, 16in, 140,000 bpd) and P5125 (Southwest Mleiha -> Mleiha, 130 km, 10in, 7,000 bpd) differ sharply in diameter and capacity (20x), and the presidency.eg source itself describes P5125's function as gathering oil FROM the Southwest Mleiha field INTO the Mleiha treatment station -- i.e. P5125 is a feeder line terminating exactly where P0572's larger outbound trunk begins. These are sequential segments of one evacuation system serving different traffic volumes, not a double-counted single pipeline. CAVEAT: the 10-inch diameter is larger than typical for a 7,000 bpd nameflow (~4-6in would be more usual); this is plausible if the line was sized for planned production growth -- a harvested (but 403-blocked, unverifiable) alwafd.news headline title from the wiki citation list ('"Agiba" raises Southwest Mleiha field production to exceed 9,500 barrels of oil per day') suggests field output has grown past the pipeline's original 7,000 bpd rating, consistent with deliberate oversizing. Not flagged as a hard concern since no source contradicts the diameter itself -- left UNRESOLVED (see fills) rather than guessed at.
